LM Studio's agentic workflow platform can now run tasks using Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion parameter, 1 million context window model from Moonshot AI. Here are the details.

Kimi K3 is now available on LM Studio Bionic

A few days ago, LM Studio announced Bionic, a new application designed for users who want to run agentic tasks with open source models.

Bionic is designed to handle coding, research, and more complex work involving the creation or modification of documents and files.

Users can run models locally or, when a task requires greater compute, leverage larger cloud-based open source models that offer longer context windows and stronger reasoning and tool calling capabilities that smaller local models currently lack.

Here is LM Studio's original announcement:

For cloud models, Bionic relies on inference services in the US with a zero data retention policy. This means requests are processed on servers in the US, and prompts, files, and model outputs are not stored once processing is complete.

Until now, users relying on cloud-based open source models had access to DeepSeek V4, Pro, GLM-5.2, Kimi K2.6, and Kimi-K2.7-Code. The company has now added Kimi K3, giving users access to what many consider the most advanced open source model currently available.

Through Bionic, Kimi K3 is priced at $3 per million input tokens, $0.30 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens.

This pricing is a stark contrast to previously available models, which ranged from $0.95 to $174 per million input tokens and $3.48 to $4.50 per million output tokens.

That said, the addition of Kimi K3 is still a welcome development, particularly for users looking to tackle more challenging tasks through LM Studio Bionic.

LM Studio Bionic is available for Mac and Windows, and you can learn more here.

Do you run local models on your Mac? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
